sources_read: .qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r10/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (Quality Checks row 44 / sheet line 45; Internal Quality Checks row 44 with Mukesh annotation; rows 42, 43; Deterministic Checks check-scoring-policy.py, check-rubric-schema.py, check-reward-weights.py) read via openpyxl read_only
evidence: Static weight analysis of frozen task (.qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r10/task). Dimension weights: tests/scoring.toml lines 5-8 functional=0.6, polish=0.2, visual=0.2, gates render/constraints=0.0 (lines 1-3), floor functional=0.05 (line 11); file is byte-identical to the frozen template rules/projects/webdev-task-template/tests/scoring.toml (both sha256 95f70d6e...bbba) and matches SKILL.md delivery profile ('functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2') and the Internal Quality Checks annotation for row 44 ('Functionality has 60 percent, and itself in functionality we define own verifier weightage'). No weight key in any [judge] block. tests/tools/score.py line 46 computes sum(w*score)/sum(w), line 48 zeroes reward unless gates and floors pass. Per-criterion weights (tests/scored/functional/judge.toml, 43 binary criteria, total 58.5): heaviest are the brief's stated 'hard part' and safety promises -- hro_stale_refused 2.5 (l.198), hro_live_board 2.5 (l.288), hro_candidate_private 2.5 (l.387), hro_bulk_all_or_none 2 (l.216), hro_undo_restores 2 (l.234), hro_undo_conflict 2 (l.243), hro_refused_put_back 2 (l.135), messaging correctness rows 1.5-2; lightest 0.5 rows are basics already proven by the constraints gate (hro_job_open l.27, hro_add_candidate l.36) or narrow edge refusals/links (hro_reject_hired, hro_undo_full, hro_activity_refusals, hro_candidate_linked). This tracks instruction.md lines 1-9 (concurrency, all-or-none, undo, live updates, candidate privacy emphasized). Polish (5 binary, total 12): hro_pol_live_board 3, hro_pol_live_thread 3, hro_pol_session_resume 2.5, hro_pol_earlier_place 2, hro_pol_failed_send 1.5 -- all are explicitly requested draft/focus/place preservation behaviours (instruction.md l.5, l.7; hireops_rules.md l.106) and the two heaviest score 0 unless the functional live update actually arrives ('If no update arrives within 15 seconds ... this row is 0'), so polish cannot be farmed by a dead app. Visual: 5 likert points=5 at equal 1.2 each (total 6), pure style, capped at 0.2 of reward. Max-contribution sanity check: functional floor requires >0.05 of 58.5 (about 3 weight units); a shell that only opens jobs/adds candidates (1.0/58.5=0.017) gets 0. A near-dead app clearing the floor (~0.06 functional) with perfect visuals and no live updates/messaging scores about 0.6*0.06+0.2*1.0+~0 polish = ~0.24, below a fully functional plain app (0.6*1.0 + polish + visual likert 1 => >=0.6). Conforming plain-styled app loses at most 0.2. Per-criterion observation (Note, not a defect): one visual likert criterion carries 1.2/6*0.2=4% of reward and the heaviest polish row 3/12*0.2=5%, versus 2.5/58.5*0.6=2.56% for the heaviest functional row; this is a consequence of the frozen template dimension shares with 43 functional criteria, the polish rows are requested behaviour dependent on functional live updates, and in aggregate functionality (0.6, plus behaviour-based polish) clearly dominates style (0.2). Not modifiable task-side without altering template-controlled policy. Runtime: raw-evidence-index.json scope states full configured grading, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent; those measurements are owned by rows 40/42 and are not needed to establish the static honesty of the weights, but no realized reward spread was measured here.
